summary:
The ACES Act of 2025, Pub. L. 119-32, mandates that the Secretary of Veterans Affairs seek to enter into an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (National Academies) to conduct a study on the prevalence and mortality of cancer among specific active duty aircrew members. 

Section 2(a)(1) establishes a statutory deadline requiring the Secretary to seek this agreement within 30 days of enactment (August 14, 2025). Under Section 2(a)(2)(A), the Secretary must finalize the agreement within 60 days of commencing negotiations. If the Secretary fails to meet this deadline, Section 2(a)(2)(B) imposes a mandatory reporting and briefing requirement: the Secretary must submit an explanatory report and timeline estimate to the Senate and House Committees on Veterans' Affairs, followed by progress briefings every 60 days until the agreement is finalized.

Section 2(b) defines the scope of the study, requiring the National Academies to:
1. Identify occupational exposures associated with covered military service, including chemicals, compounds, agents, and other phenomena;
2. Review scientific literature to determine associations between those exposures and overall cancer morbidity, overall cancer mortality, and the increased incidence or prevalence of twelve specified cancers (brain, colon and rectal, kidney, lung, melanoma skin, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreatic, prostate, testicular, thyroid, and urinary bladder cancers, plus any other cancers determined appropriate by the Secretary in consultation with the National Academies); and
3. Determine, to the extent possible, the prevalence and mortality of these cancers using available data sources. Permissible data sources include administrative and healthcare databases of the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Defense, and individual military services; the National Center for Health Statistics' national death index; and the study conducted pursuant to section 750 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Pub. L. 116-283).

Section 2(c) requires the National Academies to submit a report containing the study's results to the Secretary and the Senate and House Committees on Veterans' Affairs upon the study's conclusion. 

Section 2(d) defines the target cohort of "covered individuals" as persons who served on active duty in the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps as aircrew members of fixed-wing aircraft, explicitly including pilots, navigators, weapons systems operators, aircraft system operators, or any other crew members who regularly flew in such aircraft. The Act contains no appropriations or explicit authorizations of appropriations.
